title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity as new partnerships and budget allocations shape the landscape. Meanwhile, the specter of GEO cancellations looms large, complicating the insurance scene and raising questions about long-term viability.

themes.title: Artemis Negotiations Heat Up
themes.body: ESA's astronaut assignment for Artemis 3 is part of a broader negotiation strategy regarding roles in the Artemis program. This reflects the ongoing complexities of international collaboration in lunar exploration.

themes.title: Space Insurance Woes
themes.body: Recent GEO cancellations are making it increasingly difficult for insurers to recover losses, raising eyebrows over the sustainability of current business models. The fallout could lead to tighter underwriting practices in the sector.

themes.title: Military Space Budgets Surge
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adds a notable $1.4 billion to space resilience initiatives, signaling a robust commitment to enhancing national security through space capabilities. This trend is likely to attract more defense contractors into the fray.

themes.title: AI's Grip on Defense
themes.body: The surge in interest for 'AI for Defense' among Y Combinator startups indicates a shift towards integrating advanced technologies in military applications. This could reshape the competitive landscape as more players vie for government contracts.
